 ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

Present petition is filed by the petitioner under Article 227 of the Constitution of India for the following reliefs.
 (A) Be pleased to admit this petition.
 (B) be pleased to issue appropriate writ, order or direction, quashing and setting the judgment and award dated 6.7.2012 passed by the learned Presiding Officer, CGIT - cum - Labour Court, Ahmedabad whereby the action on the part of the bank authorities in terminating the services of the petitioner has been confirmed and

be pleased to issue appropriate writ, order or direction, holding that the action on the part of the respondent bank authorities in terminating the services of the petitioner is illegal, arbitrary and improper in the aforesaid peculiar facts and circumstances of the case.

(C) Pending admission and final disposal of this petition, be pleased to issue appropriate writ, order or direction directing the respondent bank authorities to reinstate the petitioner, subject to final outcome of the petition.
(D) Pass such orders as thought fit in the interest of justice.

(E) Be pleased to issue appropriate writ or order or direction upon the respondent bank to disburse / release all the benefits which have become due and payable to the applicant from the date of suspension i.e. 29/07/1994 till today which could have been granted to the petitioner, if the petitioner was in service as well as be pleased to direct the respondent bank to disburse / release all the retirement dues as well as all pensionary benefits to the petitioner and further be pleased to direct the respondent bank to pay all the aforementioned dues with 12% interest from the date of suspension i.e. 29/07/1994 till the date of disbursement in the interest of justice".

Brief facts of the present case, in nutshell, are as under:-

The petitioner was an employee of respondent No.1 bank and he had served on the post of the Staff Clerk in the respondent bank during 1977 to 1994 and he was serving as Staff Clerk at Lalgate branch of the respondent - bank during 1988 to 1994 and he was never allotted the work of saving bank account.
It is the case of the petitioner that he was never entrusted with the work relating to debit / credit entries and/or work relating to issuance of cheque books.
While the petitioner was serving as the Staff Clerk in the main branch of respondent - bank in Surat, he was placed under suspension by order dated 29.7.1994.

That respondent - bank issued communication and the petitioner was served with the charge-sheet dated 26.12.1994 on the allegations that one another employee of the respondent - bank Shri K.J. Adhvaryu had indulged into fraud with the bank during the period from 1988 to 1994 and it has been further alleged in the said charge-sheet that the said employee Shri Adhvaryu had committed fraud and had misappropriated huge amount from Gopipura branch of respondent - bank and had cheated bank to the tune of Rs.1,01,04,000/-.

2.2 That inquiry was held and inquiry officer had submitted his report to the disciplinary authority and, ultimately, disciplinary authority issued second show cause notice on 06.06.1996 and,
thereafter, the service of the petitioner came to be terminated by oral order.

Thereafter, the petitioner had filed an appeal before the Appellate Authority, however, without giving any opportunity of hearing to the petitioner, the appeal came to be rejected by the Appellate Authority.

That against the action of the respondent - bank, the petitioner had raised dispute, which ultimately came to be referred to the Industrial Tribunal and which came to be registered as Reference No.ITC.6/1998 (old).
It is further the case of the petitioner that in the said reference, the petitioner had raised grievance in respect of violation of principles of natural justice by the inquiry officer.
The petitioner had also raised grievance that the entire inquiry was vitiated as he was not supplied the necessary documents, which had caused prejudice to him in defending the case.
